ownership_reason: Only the per-part check in the gold sees each dot-separated part together with the simple-name predicates; the guard, the split, the range placement and the pass-through hand the name or the parts array along and cannot reject every reserved-word part with a one-line change (that needs a loop over the parts). The convention is pinned outside the gold: NodeUtil.isValidSimpleName ('a valid variable name') rejects TokenStream.isKeyword names; ProcessClosurePrimitives.verifyProvide validates each part of a dotted namespace with isValidPropertyName and ProcessClosurePrimitivesTest.testInvalidProvide rejects 'a.class'; CodeGenerator.add quotes object-literal keys that are keywords (CodePrinterTest.testPrint keeps "default" quoted) and ConvertToDottedPropertiesTest.testDoNotConvert keeps a['default']. The gold's javadoc promises valid simple names, that is, valid variable names, which 'true' is not.
